subject: Edge trust boundary & DNS ownership — handoff plan for private deployment
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-telecom.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-telecom.com, devops@acme-telecom.com
Date: 2028-02-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment — TLS termination & DNS ownership questions

Vivek,

Thanks again for the initial onboarding call last week. As we prepare for the POC in our VPC, the security team asked for a clear plan on two items before we sign the SOW:

1) Where is TLS terminated for customer-facing private endpoints? Options we have:
   - Customer edge (their load balancer / private proxy) terminates TLS and then mTLS to Redwood;
   - Redwood edge (private endpoint inside customer VPC) terminates TLS;
   - Mutual TLS maintained across both with split responsibilities.

2) DNS ownership and delegations for the private FQDNs (we currently use split-horizon for other vendors). Will Redwood hold NS records, or do we provide a CNAME/ALIAS to a Redwood-managed internal FQDN?

We attached a short inventory of existing TLS assets and hostnames. Also, our compliance team needs a short handoff playbook that says who rotates certs, who manages ACME challenges (if any), and what evidence (audit logs) you'll provide.

Attachment: acme_cert_inventory.csv (csv, 14KB)

Open to a quick working session tomorrow if that helps — Rajiv (security) and our DevOps lead can join.

Regards,
Rajiv Menon
Head of Platform Security
Acme Telecom
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-telecom.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — TLS termination & DNS ownership questions

Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up-front: we support either pattern but prefer a customer-edge TLS termination with mutual TLS between your edge and our side for the strictest isolation; we can also operate a Redwood-side termination when customers want zero TLS exposure at their edge.

I'll outline a pragmatic playbook below and propose a working session to lock the details. High-level options and tradeoffs:

A) Customer-terminates TLS (recommended for customers who want control)
   - You own public/private certs and NS records.
   - You terminate at your private LB / edge-proxy. Redwood establishes mTLS to a Redwood backend host inside your VPC (Redwood holds client certs for mutual auth).
   - Pros: clear trust boundary, no private key sharing. Cons: requires your LB to support client cert verification or mTLS passthrough.

B) Redwood-terminates TLS inside VPC (Redwood-managed private endpoint)
   - You delegate an internal DNS name (CNAME/ALIAS or NS delegation) to Redwood-managed resolver. Redwood provisions and rotates certs (ACME or Vault-backed) and exposes the endpoint inside your VPC.
   - Pros: simpler for customers that can’t run ACME/rotation. Cons: requires DNS delegation and audit/artifact sharing.

C) Split horizon / proxy hybrid
   - External client traffic hits your internal edge. For egress to Redwood we normalize with an internal mTLS hop or TLS-with-client-auth. Good for transit proxies.

Proposed deliverables for the playbook:
 - Ownership table (DNS, cert issuance, rotation, proof of rotation logs)
 - TLS termination diagram for chosen option
 - Minimal runbook snippets for CSR handoff or ACME challenge (http-01/ dns-01)
 - Audit evidence we will provide (signed rotation events + KMS key IDs)

Can you confirm your preference (A/B/C)? If you prefer A, we need the LB capability details and a template for the CSR and mTLS CA bundle. If B, we’ll request a short NS/CNAME delegation and provide the Redwood-side CSR/rotation schedule.

I can take first pass on the playbook and circulate v1 by EOD tomorrow. Would you like to schedule a 30m working session?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-telecom.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-13T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment — TLS termination & DNS ownership questions

Rajiv —

Putting some concrete checkboxes here from an ops/security handoff perspective (this will be in the playbook PDF):

Checklist for option A (Customer terminates TLS + mTLS to Redwood):
 - Customer provides reachable SANs and LB capability notes (supports client cert auth, SNI preservation, TCP passthrough).
 - Customer supplies CA bundle for Redwood client certs or agrees to accept Redwood client certs signed by our CA.
 - Redwood provides client certs (rotated quarterly) and a single trusted CA public key and KID for audit.
 - Redirect/health-check endpoints: we’ll need 1 writable internal path for health+metrics (non-prod path included).
 - DNS: no delegation needed; provide internal hostnames so we can set up monitoring and local resolver rules.

Checklist for option B (Redwood terminates inside your VPC):
 - Customer creates a private zone and delegates either: 
     * full NS delegation for a subdomain we will manage inside your resolver, OR
     * a single CNAME/ALIAS per endpoint pointing to redwood-private.<region>.internal (your resolver must support CNAME to internal host).
 - Customer grants Redwood a short-lived role to add TXT records if dns-01 ACME is used OR we use CSR handoff for an offline CA flow.
 - Required artifacts we will send: cert rotation schedule, access log sample, rotation audit list, and signed attestation of key rollover.

Operational notes:
 - If using ACME dns-01, many enterprise DNS providers require an automation account. We prefer CSR handoff for air-gapped hosts.
 - We can provide a tiny sidecar (ACME agent) that you run in a customer-managed cluster to present challenges locally; this avoids DNS delegations but pushes an agent to your infra.

Attached: initial handoff playbook draft (redwood-handoff-playbook-v1.pdf). I included templates for CSR, rotation schedule, and a short matrix that maps who does what.

Attachment: redwood-handoff-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 45 pages)

If this looks good, I can convert the checklist into a short Trello/Jira backlog for the POC run.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vivek —

Thanks for the clear playbook. We reviewed internally and prefer option A for the POC: customer-terminates TLS at our edge and we accept mTLS from Redwood. Key follow-ups from our side:
 - Our LB (F5) supports client cert verification but we need the exact cert profile and rolling window details.
 - For the CSR handoff: we prefer not to run ACME agents. Please send the CSR template and the expected cert subject/SANs.
 - Two compliance asks: can you provide a sample rotation audit entry and the KMS key ID that signs the client certs? Also we need an operator-run document for emergency revocation.

We’ll schedule the working session for Wednesday 11am PT.

Regards,
Rajiv
